summary.one_liner: gping is a command-line tool that works like ping but draws the round-trip times as a live graph, and can also graph how long commands take to run.
summary.what_it_does: It pings one or more hosts and plots the response times on a terminal graph, so several targets can be compared side by side. With the --cmd flag it instead graphs the execution time of arbitrary commands over repeated runs. Hosts can be IPs or names, and -4/-6 force IPv4 or IPv6 resolution. Shorthands such as aws:eu-west-1 ping specific AWS cloud regions; the README says only aws is currently supported. Display options include custom colours (hex #RRGGBB or named colours), a configurable graph buffer length in seconds, adjustable watch interval, simple ASCII dot graphics instead of braille, margins, choice of network interface, and clearing the graph on exit.
use_cases: graph ping latency to several servers at once
monitor connection quality to a host over time
graph how long a shell command takes to run
notable: Graphs ping times for multiple hosts on one terminal chart
--cmd mode graphs execution time of any command
Custom colours via hex codes or named colours
Braille graphics by default, with a simple dot mode
caveats: Cargo install requires rustc 1.67.0 or greater
Cloud region shorthand currently supports only aws
